text:
anya: Heads-up — intake for Harbor-7b (community checkpoint) — curious about an odd clause in the license mentioning export restrictions for certain countries. Can legal/ops advise?

mike: pinging @linda for legal + @kevin for infra impact. Quick summary: model weights released with CC-BY-ish header but an addendum says 'no deployment to sanctioned territories' and references dual-use controls.

linda: thanks @mike. Can you drop the license header here? small snippet is enough.

mike: ```
License: CommunityModel v1.0
Redistribution allowed for research and commercial use, except where prohibited by export control or sanctions law.
See addendum: export_clause_alpha
```

linda: ok — that wording is ambiguous. "Prohibited by export control" is generic; we need to know whether the authors intentionally restricted specific countries or whether it's boilerplate. If it's a blanket national-security restriction, that could block Hosted usage in some regions.

anya: it's not just hosted — team wants to test quantized variants on Dedicated and Private. If export triggers apply, on-prem deployments might be fine but we need compliance docs.

kevin: operational note: our on-prem bundle includes a binary that runs quantized kernels. If license restricts distribution of modified weights to certain countries, we may need geo-gating and extra attestation in the install script. That adds ~2 sprints to private rollout.

linda: immediate ask: mike, ask upstream (or repo owner) whether addendum names specific jurisdictions or refers to statutes. Also ask if they require an export license for redistribution/modification. If they name statutes (ITAR, EAR), escalate to security/compliance.

mike: filed an issue and linked the commit: https://github.com/harbor-ai/harbor-weights/issues/412 — their maintainer replied: "we included a conservative clause referencing 'applicable export controls' but did not list countries; we're open to clarifying."

license-bot: auto-scan results: harbor-7b-v1.tar.gz -> detected permissive header + unidentified addendum token. Risk: "ambiguous export language" -> triage required.

linda: good. Next step is to get a written clarification; until then classify as "conditional" for hosted and dedicated. For Private (customer-managed) we can allow evals if customers sign a risk attestation — legal will prepare a short form.

anya: parallel technical thread: mike/kevin — can you run a quick quantization experiment (int8+AWQ) to profile quality delta? We need baseline with HF fp16 -> quantized on one seq-length distribution we care about (SLA: 512 tokens).

kevin: plan: run A/B on prompt set from core-evals (subset: 500 prompts), measure avg perplexity proxy + Rouge/EM for structured tasks. Also capture latency p50/p95 on p4d and T4. I can get results by EOD tomorrow.

mike: will add test harness: `scripts/quant_eval.sh --model harbor-7b --q awq --promptset core-evals/harbor-subset.json --out results/harbor-awq.json` — will push logs here.

anya: include kv-cache footprint and batch-size effects — our batching heuristics might need adjusting for quantized kernels.

kevin: noted. Also running a quick smoke to ensure no forbidden header is embedded in the weight package (weird but happened before where license.txt ended up in the load path).

linda: one more compliance nit: some contributors included a CLA that says derivatives must preserve attribution and cannot be used for military targeting. We need to map that to our TOS; if it's enforceable we might be blocked from selling Dedicated with that model.

mike: summarizing action items: 1) get upstream clarification about export clause (mike) 2) legal draft attestation for Private evals (linda) 3) quantization + perf/quality report (kevin + mike) 4) license-bot watchlist until clarification (license-bot).

anya: thanks. If quantization regressions are small (<2% on primary metrics) and license clarification is reasonable (no named-country ban), we proceed with a soft onboard: internal-only tests on Dedicated, no public hosted rollout.

kevin: uploaded preliminary numbers: p50 latency down 30% on T4 with int8-awq, quality drop ~1.8% on our normalized metric. Added results: results/1712345678-harbor-quant-quick.json

mike: upstream replied in the GH issue: "we can replace the ambiguous sentence with: 'subject to applicable law' and remove the addendum, CC-BY-2.0 style." They also offered a CLA amendment to permit enterprise redistribution if credited.

linda: if they remove the addendum and grant enterprise redistribution explicitly, legal will sign off for Dedicated and Private. Hosted still needs export due diligence but likely fine.

anya: ok let's freeze this intake as conditional-approved. Mike, copy links to the GH clarification and quant results into the intake ticket and set priority to P2.

mike: done -> https://redwood-internal/issue/ONB-742 (links to GH + results). Setting watchers: @linda, @kevin, @anya.

license-bot: watchlist update: harbor-7b cleared on 1712346890 after upstream edit.

anya: closing thread for now. Reopen if the formal CLA amendment diverges from the gist or quant regressions exceed 3% in extended evals. :white_check_mark:
